//: Models that are not on this machine. Copy this file to remotes.json and edit.
Each key is the alias shown in /model. Fields:
baseUrl    required. The API root, WITHOUT the path (no /v1/messages, no /v1/chat/completions).
api        "anthropic" (default) or "openai". Anthropic is passed straight through; openai
is translated in both directions by src/openai.mjs, which is what makes a
Chat-Completions-only provider such as build.nvidia.com usable from Claude Code.
model      the model id sent upstream. Defaults to the alias.
apiKey     a literal key. Prefer apiKeyEnv unless the file is safe to hold it.
apiKeyEnv  name of an environment variable holding the key.
ctx        the window to advertise. The session uses the SMALLEST in the picker,
so a small number here drags every local model down with it.
enabled    set false to keep an entry configured but out of the picker.
label      display name in the picker. Defaults to the alias.
maxOutput  clamp max_tokens. Omit for hosted models - they are fast enough not to need it.
fallback   alias, or list of aliases, to try when this one answers 429 or 5xx or refuses the
connection. Chains follow: a fallback's own fallback is tried after it. A hop is
only retried while nothing of the answer has reached Claude Code yet. Once the whole
chain is exhausted the proxy walks it again a few times with backoff, so a rate
limit measured over a window resolves itself instead of failing the turn.
extra      body fields merged in after translation (openai only): reasoning_effort, seed, ...
reasoning  what to do with reasoning_content (openai only): "think" (default) makes a real
Anthropic thinking block, "text" folds it into the answer, "drop" discards it.
path       override the upstream path (openai only). Default /v1/chat/completions.
remotes.json is gitignored, because it may hold a key.

opus-5.label: Claude Opus 5 (your subscription)
opus-5.note: No key: "auth": "claude-subscription" reads the OAuth token from Claude Code's own credential store at call time. Run 'claude' once if it has expired. Copy this block for sonnet-5 (claude-sonnet-5) and haiku-4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001).

kimi-k3-nvidia.label: Kimi K3 (NVIDIA NIM)
kimi-k3-nvidia.note: build.nvidia.com is OpenAI Chat Completions only, so this entry needs api:"openai". One key allows about one request in flight; Claude Code fires side-requests alongside the main turn, so a second key is what keeps a session from stalling on 429.

kimi-k3-nvidia-fallback1.label: Kimi K3 (NVIDIA NIM, key 2)
kimi-k3-nvidia-fallback1.note: Same endpoint and model, different key. It shows in /model on its own AND backs the entry above. Each key points at the NEXT one rather than the primary listing them all, so adding a key is one edit.

kimi-k3-nvidia-fallback2.label: Kimi K3 (NVIDIA NIM, key 3)
kimi-k3-nvidia-fallback2.note: End of the chain. Free-tier quota is per key and measured over a window, so three keys is roughly three times the budget - not just three times the concurrency.

qwen3.8-27b-tpu.label: Qwen3.8-27B bf16 (Kaggle TPU v5e-8)
qwen3.8-27b-tpu.note: python launch.py serve  in ~/Projects/kaggle-tpu-lab prints the URL and key. Bearer ONLY - this server rejects x-api-key, hence authStyle. Full bf16 weights, no quantization, ~130 tok/s.

qwen3.8-27b-kaggle.label: Qwen3.8-27B (Kaggle T4x2)
qwen3.8-27b-kaggle.note: Printed by kaggle/claudelocal-kaggle.ipynb. New URL and key every session.

glm-4.7-flash-kaggle.label: GLM-4.7-Flash (Kaggle T4x2)
glm-4.7-flash-kaggle.note: Same tunnel as the Qwen entry - llama-swap routes on the model id.

glm-5.3.label: GLM-5.3 (Z.ai)
glm-5.3.note: 744B-A40B. Far too large to run locally at any quantization - this is the hosted model.

kimi-k3.label: Kimi K3 (Moonshot)
kimi-k3.note: 2.8T-A104B. Its 1-bit dynamic GGUF is 594 GB, so hosted is the only option.

lan-box.label: llama-server on the LAN
lan-box.note: No key needed on a trusted network - omit apiKey and apiKeyEnv entirely.
